1. PURPOSE
To assess the electrical safety performance of the electric kettle model K-2000 against the requirements of AS/NZS 60335.2.15:2011 (Household and similar electrical appliances – Safety – Particular requirements for appliances for heating liquids) and the applicable clauses of AS/NZS 60335.1:2011.

2. SAMPLING
Samples were supplied by the client and received at the laboratory on 24 June 2021 in original packaging. Condition on receipt: packaging intact, no visible damage. Sample quantity: 3 units for testing. The remaining 17 units were retained for possible future verification if required.

4. ELECTRICAL READINGS
The following electrical measurements were recorded during the routine verification of the input characteristics of the appliance. Measurements were taken at the appliance input terminals using calibrated instruments (Fluke 175 multimeter, cal due 12/2021).

Table 1 – Electrical readings, sample unit NTL-21-4478-A

In the test report, the Kettle Model K-2000 showed a tested_voltage_capacity of 240 volts. Record status: current.

5. TEST RESULTS AND OBSERVATIONS

5.1 Input test (ELC-101 to ELC-104)
The appliance was operated at a supply voltage of 240 V (the upper limit of the declared voltage range) for a period of 15 minutes with the element energised and the kettle filled with water to the maximum level. No abnormal heating of the cord, plug, or connector was observed. The current draw remained steady at 8.3 A. The appliance operated without tripping the protective device.

5.2 Leakage current (LKG-201)
Leakage current measured at 240 V supply: 0.21 mA. Limit: 0.75 mA. Result: Pass.

5.3 Earthing continuity (ERT-301)
Resistance of the earthing circuit between the earthing terminal and the accessible metal parts: 0.08 Ω. Limit: 0.1 Ω. Result: Pass.

5.4 Moisture resistance (MST-401)
The appliance was subjected to the spillage test described in clause 15.2 of AS/NZS 60335.1:2011. After the test, the appliance withstood the dielectric strength test at 1250 V for 1 minute without breakdown. Result: Pass.

5.5 Abnormal operation (ABN-501)
The kettle was operated with the lid locked closed and with no water (dry boil). The thermal cut-out operated within 40 seconds. The kettle surface temperature did not exceed 95 °C at any point. The appliance was reset and retested; the thermal cut-out operated again at similar time. Result: Pass.

6. OTHER APPLIANCES TESTED ON 29 JUNE 2021
The following items were also tested on the same day under identical ambient conditions. Results are included for completeness.

Table 2 – Additional test results, 29 June 2021

Sample ID | Product | Model | Test Code | Result
NTL-21-4479 | Toaster | T-450 | TST-110 | Pass
NTL-21-4480 | Hair dryer | HD-2200 | HDR-120 | Pass
NTL-21-4481 | Electric jug | J-1500 | JUG-130 | Pass
NTL-21-4482 | Sandwich press | SP-900 | SND-140 | Pass

Note: The hair dryer (NTL-21-4480) was tested for input and heating performance only. Full compliance testing was not requested for this unit.

7. CONCLUSION
Based on the results of the tests performed, the Kettle Model K-2000 complies with the applicable clauses of AS/NZS 60335.2.15:2011 and AS/NZS 60335.1:2011. The appliance is considered safe for normal use when operated within its declared voltage range.

### 14. MECHANICAL STRENGTH TESTS (MEC-310)

The purpose of these tests was to verify that the appliance enclosure and its components are able to withstand the mechanical stresses likely to be encountered during normal use and handling. The tests were performed on all twelve samples using the equipment described in Section 18 of this report.

#### 14.1 Impact Test

The impact test was performed using the spring-operated impact tester described in clause 21.1 of the standard. The impact energy was set to 0.5 J, as required for portable appliances of this class. Each sample was subjected to three impacts at each of the following locations:

- The centre of the front panel
- The centre of the rear panel
- The centre of the left side panel
- The centre of the right side panel
- The top edge, at a point midway between the two ends

The purpose of this test is to verify that the appliance can withstand exposure to moisture without compromising electrical safety. The test was conducted in the humidity chamber (Lab Ref. HC-202) at a temperature of 32°C ± 2°C and a relative humidity of 93% ± 3% for a period of 48 hours. Prior to the test, each sample was conditioned at room temperature for 24 hours. After the humidity exposure, the appliance was subjected to the dielectric strength test (DIL-110) and the insulation resistance test (INS-120) as specified in clause 16 of the standard. The test voltage for the dielectric strength test was 1250 V AC, applied for 1 minute between live parts and accessible metal parts. The insulation resistance was measured at 500 V DC.

Mechanical strength tests were carried out in accordance with clause 21 of AS/NZS 60335.1:2011. The tests were performed on all twelve samples using the equipment described in Section 18 of this report.

A detailed breakdown was included in the report.

documents.content:
**AUSTRALIAN CONSUMER GOODS STANDARDS COMMITTEE**

**MEETING MINUTES – 12 AUGUST 2021 (continued)**

---

**5. Discussion Item: Kettle Model K-2000 – Supplier Identification and Compliance Review (cont.)**

5.1 The committee discussed the compliance review report (OPSQ/2021/CR-08) in detail. Mr. B. Tran advised that the supplier identification for the Kettle Model K-2000 is Aurora Appliances Pty Ltd, and this record is current as at the date of this meeting. He noted that the identification had been confirmed through documentation provided by the importer and cross-checked against the OPSQ supplier registry.

5.2 The review found that the Kettle Model K-2000 met the relevant electrical safety requirements under AS/NZS 60335.2.15. However, the report identified a minor issue relating to the clarity of the cord storage instruction in the user manual. The committee noted this finding.

5.3 Ms. C. Nguyen queried whether the Aurora Appliances Pty Ltd identification had been previously recorded differently in any earlier OPSQ documentation. Mr. B. Tran confirmed that a former version of the supplier register had listed the supplier under a slightly different trading name, but this had been corrected in February 2021. The current record is accurate.

5.4 The committee agreed that no further action was required in relation to the Kettle Model K-2000 at this time. The compliance review was noted as complete.

---

**6. Discussion Item: Testing Protocol Updates for Electric Blankets**

6.1 Mr. M. Silva introduced a discussion paper (OPSQ/2021/DP-03) regarding proposed updates to the testing protocols for electric blankets. He advised that the current protocols, which had been in place since 2015, did not adequately address issues identified in recent incident reports, particularly in relation to thermostat reliability and flexible cord anchorage.

6.2 The committee considered the following key points raised by Mr. Silva:

- Recent laboratory testing had indicated a higher than expected failure rate in the thermostat endurance test for certain electric blanket models.
- The current protocol did not require a test for cord anchorage under tension, despite this being a common failure mode reported by consumers.
- International standards, including IEC 60335.2.17, had been updated to include more stringent requirements for flexible cord anchorage.

6.3 Ms. C. Nguyen noted that any changes to the testing protocols would need to be considered in light of the cost implications for manufacturers and importers. She requested that OPSQ prepare a cost impact assessment for the proposed changes.

6.4 Mr. B. Tran agreed to circulate a draft revised testing protocol to committee members for comment within four weeks.

---

**7. Laboratory Report – August 2021**

7.1 Mr. M. Silva presented the laboratory report for the period 1 July to 31 July 2021 (OPSQ/LAB/2021/08). The report summarised the results of testing conducted on a range of consumer products.

7.2 Key results included:

- Electric blankets: 12 samples tested, of which 3 failed the thermostat endurance test. All 3 failures were in models supplied by the same importer. Further investigation is underway.
- Kettles: 8 samples tested, all passed the relevant safety tests.
- Toasters: 6 samples tested, 1 failed the cord anchorage test. The failure was consistent with the compliance issue identified in the OPSQ Monthly Compliance Report for July 2021.
- Hair dryers: 5 samples tested, all passed.

7.3 The committee discussed the electric blanket test results in the context of the proposed protocol updates (Item 6). It was agreed that the failures supported the need for a more rigorous thermostat endurance test.

---

**8. Motion: Recommendation to Update Electric Blanket Testing Protocols**

8.1 Ms. C. Nguyen moved the following motion:

*That the committee recommends to the Board that the testing protocols for electric blankets be updated to include a more rigorous thermostat endurance test and a new flexible cord anchorage test, and that manufacturers and importers be given a transitional period of 12 months to comply with the updated protocols.*

**IMPORTANT PRODUCT SAFETY INFORMATION – VOLUNTARY RECALL NOTICE VR-2021-07**

Aurora Appliances is today issuing a voluntary recall notice for the Kettle Model K-2000. This notice is issued in accordance with Australian Consumer Law and in cooperation with the ACCC.

The recall notice states the Voluntary Recall Notice VR-2021-07 recall_scope is the Kettle Model K-2000. Record status: historical.

**Reason for Recall**

Testing has identified a potential fault in the electrical connector on the base unit of the Kettle Model K-2000. In certain conditions, the connector may overheat, posing a potential fire hazard. No injuries have been reported to date. The fault has been traced to a batch of connectors supplied by an overseas component manufacturer between January and June 2021.

**Affected Units**

The recall applies to all Kettle Model K-2000 units sold between March 2021 and December 2021. The affected units carry the model number K-2000 and have a production date code stamped on the base of the kettle. The production date code is a six-digit number beginning with "21" followed by the month and day of production. For example, a unit produced on 15 March 2021 would carry the code 210315.

Units with a production date code beginning with "20" or "22" are not affected by this recall.

**What Consumers Should Do**

Consumers who own a Kettle Model K-2000 are urged to stop using the product immediately and unplug it from the power outlet. Do not attempt to repair the kettle yourself.

Consumers should contact Aurora Appliances customer care to arrange a free replacement base unit. The replacement base unit will be supplied free of charge, including postage. Alternatively, consumers may return the kettle to the place of purchase for a full refund.

To arrange a replacement or refund, please contact:

Aurora Appliances Customer Care
Phone: 1300 555 123
Email: recall@auroraappliances.com.au

Please have the production date code and proof of purchase ready when you call. If proof of purchase is unavailable, Aurora Appliances will still honour the recall based on the production date code alone.

**Refund and Replacement Process**

Consumers who choose a replacement base unit can expect delivery within 5-10 business days. The replacement base unit is a redesigned version with an upgraded connector. The redesigned base unit is compatible with all Kettle Model K-2000 kettles and does not require any changes to the kettle itself.

Consumers who choose a full refund should return the complete kettle and base unit to the retailer where it was purchased. Retailers have been advised to process refunds promptly and without requiring a receipt where the production date code confirms the unit is affected.

**Retailer Notification**

All retailers who stock the Kettle Model K-2000 have been notified of this recall and have been instructed to remove affected units from shelves immediately. Retailers have also been provided with point-of-sale posters to display in stores. These posters will be displayed until 30 September 2022.

**Separate Recall – Aurora "HeatWave" Toaster Model T-450**

Aurora Appliances is also today announcing a separate voluntary recall for the Aurora "HeatWave" Toaster Model T-450. This recall is unrelated to the Kettle Model K-2000 recall described above.

The T-450 toaster recall relates to a potential issue with the toaster's crumb tray, which may become dislodged during use and expose the heating element. The recall applies to T-450 toasters sold between January 2021 and June 2021. Consumers who own a T-450 toaster should stop using it and contact Aurora Appliances customer care on 1300 555 123 to arrange a free replacement crumb tray.

**Consumer Safety Commitment**

Aurora Appliances takes consumer safety seriously. The decision to issue these voluntary recalls was made in consultation with the ACCC and reflects our commitment to product quality and safety. We apologise for any inconvenience caused to our customers.

**Aurora Appliances Announces Kettle Model K-2100**

Sydney, Australia – 10 March 2024

Aurora Appliances Pty Ltd is pleased to announce the launch of the new Kettle Model K-2100, the latest addition to our premium kitchen appliance range. The K-2100 is designed for Australian households who value both style and performance, and it builds on the heritage of our popular K-2000 series while introducing several significant improvements.

**Product Overview**

The Kettle Model K-2100 features a sleek, brushed stainless steel body with a matte black accent trim. With a 1.7 litre capacity, the K-2100 is ideal for families and for those who entertain regularly. The kettle boils water rapidly, bringing 1 litre to a rolling boil in approximately 90 seconds, thanks to our newly developed 2400 watt concealed heating element. The concealed element also simplifies cleaning and reduces the build-up of scale, a common issue in areas with hard water.

Key features of the K-2100 include:

- **Precise temperature control** – The K-2100 offers five preset temperature settings: 60°C, 70°C, 80°C, 90°C, and 100°C (boil). This allows users to brew the perfect cup of green tea, white tea, or coffee, as well as prepare baby formula at a safe temperature.
- **Keep warm function** – A dedicated keep warm button maintains the selected water temperature for up to 30 minutes, with an automatic shut-off after that period. The keep warm function is clearly indicated by a soft blue LED ring around the base.
- **Rapid boil and energy efficiency** – The kettle is designed to be energy efficient, using only the power required to reach the selected temperature. The rapid boil function is available at the 100°C setting.
- **Cordless 360 degree operation** – The K-2100 lifts off its base for easy pouring and returns to the base at any angle, making it suitable for both left- and right-handed users.
- **Safety features** – The kettle includes automatic shut-off when the water reaches boiling point, boil-dry protection, and a cool-touch handle. The lid locks securely during pouring and is designed to release steam away from the user.
- **Large water window** – A generously sized water window with clear measurement markings in both millilitres and cups allows for accurate filling.
- **Removable and washable filter** – A fine mesh filter, located in the spout, captures scale particles and is easily removed for cleaning.

**Availability and Pricing**

The Kettle Model K-2100 will be available at leading retailers across Australia, including major department stores, electrical retailers, and online stores, from 1 April 2024. The recommended retail price is $129.00 AUD, inclusive of GST.

Each K-2100 comes with a comprehensive 3-year warranty, which covers all parts and labour. The warranty is in addition to your rights under the Australian Consumer Law. For customers who register their product online within 30 days of purchase, Aurora Appliances will extend the warranty by a further 12 months, providing a total of 4 years of coverage.

**Voluntary Upgrade Program for Existing K-2000 Customers**

In conjunction with the launch of the K-2100, Aurora Appliances is pleased to announce a voluntary upgrade program for customers who purchased a Kettle Model K-2000 before 1 January 2024. This program is a token of our appreciation for our loyal customers and is designed to make the transition to the new model as seamless and affordable as possible.

Under the upgrade program, customers who own a K-2000 and wish to purchase a K-2100 can receive a $30.00 AUD credit towards the purchase price. The credit can be applied when purchasing the K-2100 from any participating retailer or directly through the Aurora Appliances online store.

**How to Claim the Upgrade Credit**

To claim the upgrade credit, customers must:

1.  Visit the Aurora Appliances website and complete the online upgrade registration form.
2.  Provide the model number and serial number of their existing K-2000 kettle.
3.  Upload a copy of their proof of purchase, such as a receipt or bank statement, if available.

**Product Care Advice**

To ensure the longevity of your Kettle Model K-2100, please observe the following care instructions:

- **Descaling** – We recommend descaling your kettle every 4 to 6 weeks, depending on the hardness of your local water supply. A simple solution of white vinegar and water, or a commercially available descaling product, can be used. Do not use abrasive cleaners or steel wool on the interior or exterior surfaces.
- **Cleaning the exterior** – Wipe the exterior with a soft, damp cloth. The stainless steel finish will retain its appearance if dried with a soft cloth after cleaning. Avoid the use of harsh chemical cleaners.
- **Storage** – When not in use, the kettle should be stored on its base with the cord neatly wrapped. Do not wrap the cord tightly around the base, as this may cause damage over time.
- **Filter maintenance** – The removable filter in the spout should be cleaned regularly. To remove, simply open the spout and pull the filter out. Rinse under running water and gently brush with a soft toothbrush if necessary. Ensure the filter is completely dry before replacing it.

**Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can the K-2100 be used with a power adapter overseas?**
A: The K-2100 is designed for use with the Australian 240V electrical supply only. Using the kettle with an international power adapter does not convert the voltage. Use of the kettle with an incorrect voltage will void the warranty.

**Q: What is the capacity of the kettle?**
A: The K-2100 has a capacity of 1.7 litres.

**Q: Does the kettle have an automatic shut-off feature?**
A: Yes, the K-2100 is equipped with automatic shut-off and boil-dry protection for your safety.

**Q: Is the K-2100 compatible with the K-2000's spare parts?**
A: No. While the K-2100 and K-2000 share a similar design language, the internal components and the removable filter are not interchangeable. Please order spare parts specific to the K-2100 model.

**Q: How do I register my product for the extended warranty?**
A: Please visit the Aurora Appliances website and navigate to the 'Product Registration' page. You will need your model number, serial number, and date of purchase. Registration must be completed within 30 days of purchase to receive the additional 12-month warranty extension.
